text:
Maria (CS): quick sync — Saffron dedicated pool bring-up tomorrow. main asks: quota planning, autoscale policy, and a short load test. goal: no >2% error rate at 95th latency under committed throughput.
Eugene (SRE): noted. what's the committed qps/token budget again?
Maria (CS): they committed 200 rps steady, bursts to 600 for 10m windows. token budget ~1.2M tokens/day. renewal flagged if >3 SLO misses in 30d, so we want conservative rollout.
Sam (Eng-Infra): cool. suggest canary ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 3 ramps, 30m each, with health checks. autoscale policy proposal: scale-up at 70% GPU util, scale-down after 10m at <40%. fallback to hosted model if capacity tight.
Jess (PM): add manual holdpoints after each ramp + CS signoff. capture enablement feedback in ticket CS-1907.
Alex (Saffron): can we keep burst window longer? some campaigns are 20m. also need IP allowlist ahead of go-live.
Maria (CS): we can extend burst to 20m for the first week. Sam to confirm warmup time. Alex — please share CIDR by EOD.
Sam (Eng-Infra): warmup estimate: 45m for KV priming at their prompt distributions unless we preload with synthetic prefixes. recommend prefix-cache prime job during maintenance window.
Eugene (SRE): load test plan attached inline. small quick test first: 10m at 50% traffic, then full load 20m. If errors spike, rollback rule: immediate 30% traffic cut and open incident page.
Sam (Eng-Infra): load test script (k6)
```
import http from 'k6/http';
import { sleep } from 'k6';
export let options = { vus: 250, duration: '20m' };
export default function () {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', JSON.stringify({prompt: 'warmup'}), {headers: {'Authorization':'Bearer X'}});
  sleep(0.2);
}
```
Maria (CS): schedule: canary start 2025-11-05T14:00Z. runbook owner: @Eugene, rollout owner: @Sam, customer enablement: @Maria.
Jess (PM): checklist items for go/no-go: quota mapping, CIDR, rollout policy in console, monitoring alerts live, SLO dashboard link. I'll post the checklist in the ticket.
Eugene (SRE): monitoring hooks: token-level cost, 95th latency, GPU util, 5xx rate. threshold alerts set. also adding a regression check to compare model outputs on a small eval set pre/post warmup.
Alex (Saffron): we appreciate the eval — want to ensure no quality regressions. we'll validate with our dev team during the canary.
Maria (CS): note on renewal risk: if first-week SLOs exceed error thresholds, we should trigger an executive outreach cadence. prefer we avoid that by conservative ramp and extra priming.
Sam (Eng-Infra): deploy-bot says pool creation started.
deploy-bot: pool saffron-dedicated created (id: pool-7a3f). warming worker instances now.
Eugene (SRE): I'll run prefix priming job after pool is at READY. command I'll run: `priming-run --pool pool-7a3f --script warmup-prefixes.json`
Maria (CS): Alex — can you confirm availability for a 30m enablement call during the canary?
Alex (Saffron): yes, 14:30Z after first ramp. adding our infra lead @Priya to the invite.
Jess (PM): capture feedback template: 1) latency observations, 2) error patterns, 3) hallucination/regression notes, 4) cost surprises. put answers in CS-1907.
Sam (Eng-Infra): one more: autoscale policy will have a hard cap at their reserved capacity to avoid overcommit. good to note for finance.
Maria (CS): thanks — I'll send the final runbook and the checklist in this thread. small follow-ups: Alex to send CIDR, Sam to confirm priming time, Eugene to set monitors.
Eugene (SRE): will do. planning to run the first short smoke test at 13:30Z tomorrow.
Maria (CS): perfect. closing notes: low-lift customer enablement docs linked here: https://redwood.internal/onboarding/saffron-dedicated. I'll add the Q&A after the call. :party_parrot: 
Alex (Saffron): thanks all — see you tomorrow.
Maria (CS): thanks — marking as go-ready unless anyone raises blockers by EOD.
